text.title: Go Backend Development Patterns Core Rules
text.summary: 14 testable rules every Go Backend Development Patterns application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: Layout MUST follow `cmd/<bin>` + `internal/<feature>` + `pkg/<lib>`; no other top-level dirs without ADR.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Go community layout (golang-standards repo + critiques). Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Handler imports service interface; service imports repository interface; repository never imports up.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Hexagonal architecture. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Every public function that crosses a layer or does I/O takes `context.Context` as first arg. Never capture `gin.Context` inside a goroutine — derive `ctx := c.Request.Context()` and extract params/headers BEFORE spawning.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Go blog + context docs. Context carries cancellation, deadlines and trace ids; `gin.Context` is request-scoped and not thread-safe, so capturing it in a goroutine is a data race plus a request-context leak. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Errors crossing layer boundaries MUST be `*apperror.AppError` (wrapped with `%w`), never bare `errors.New`.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: go-error-handling methodology. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: main() MUST listen for SIGINT/SIGTERM, `Shutdown(ctx)` HTTP server, wait on `WaitGroup`, then exit.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: stdlib net/http docs. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Interfaces MUST be defined where consumed (handler defines `UserService`, `internal/service` defines `UserRepository`), never at the producer. `internal/repository` ships concrete types only and MUST NOT declare `type X interface`.

rationale.source: Go proverb 'accept interfaces, return structs' + effective-go

rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Go proverb 'accept interfaces, return structs'. Consumer-side interfaces break import cycles and make mocking straightforward — the test supplies a mock satisfying the interface without importing the real implementation. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Background goroutines MUST be scoped to a `context.Context` and tracked in a `WaitGroup`.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: go-goroutines + goleak docs. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Bind HTTP input into separate `*Request` structs. NEVER bind directly into a domain model struct.
rule.rationale: Domain models carry fields external input must never set — ids, timestamps, internal flags. DTO separation is what enforces that boundary. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: `cmd/api/main.go` MUST stay wiring-only (config → deps → router → server); no business logic, and under 50 lines.
rule.rationale: Agents bloat main.go when unconstrained because that is where the program visibly runs. A thin main keeps every layer independently testable. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Use small, single-purpose middlewares (Gin/Echo/chi). Business logic MUST NOT live in middleware.
rule.rationale: Small middlewares compose cleanly and are easier for agents to read and extend; business logic hidden in a middleware is invisible to the handler that owns the endpoint.

rule.statement: Use `ShouldBindJSON` (returns error), never `BindJSON` (writes 400 and aborts). Declare validation with `binding` struct tags.
rule.rationale: `ShouldBind*` lets the handler return the canonical error response; `BindJSON` aborts the chain and bypasses the ErrorHandler middleware, so the error never reaches central mapping or metrics. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Exactly ONE ErrorHandler middleware maps `AppError` to HTTP status. Handlers call `c.Error(err)` and return — never `c.JSON` for an error path.
rule.rationale: Centralised mapping is what makes the error shape consistent across endpoints and stops HTTP status logic being duplicated in every handler; it is also the only place error logging and metrics can be complete. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: A worker `Pool` uses a buffered jobs channel and context-aware workers; `Pool.Submit` MUST `select` on both the jobs channel and `ctx.Done()`.
rule.rationale: A blocking send into a full buffer with no ctx awareness deadlocks the moment the caller is cancelled, and graceful shutdown then hangs. The select pattern drains cleanly. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Default worker count is `runtime.NumCPU()`. Close the jobs channel once all jobs are sent and let workers drain their `range` loop.
rule.rationale: Closing the channel is the exit signal — it removes the need for a second stop channel and guarantees every queued job is processed before the worker returns.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit an artefact passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions hold and no duplicate exists.

rule.statement: Skip; surface the missing precondition; do not synthesize.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.

rule.statement: Update the existing artefact in place (bump version, refresh last_reviewed).
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when a duplicate is found.
